teams.heading: Fiji to host Samoa, Tonga and Australia A in World Cup warm-up
teams.body: The inaugural Quad Series, set for July next year, will run in place of the Pacific Nations Cup, Fiji Rugby Union chief executive Koli Sewabu has confirmed. He said Fiji needed more quality matches before the World Cup, with Australian Government funding making it possible. Suva is the preferred venue, though Sewabu said "it'll all depend too on availability of accommodation." Two further matches, involving Japan and then South Africa, are locked in, the second about two weeks before the tournament starts.

lead.why: It is the only fresh reported event about Fiji's men's XV; the other new items are Italian player comments.

teams.heading: England to wear Moody's 'Front Up' MND boots against All Blacks
teams.body: Lewis Moody, the 2003 World Cup winner who captained England at the 2011 tournament, says he has been buoyed by the squad's backing. Players will wear training tops and specially painted boots promoting his 'Front Up' campaign at Saturday's test against New Zealand. Diagnosed with MND last year, Moody is asking supporters to walk one of 175 routes, each 26 miles long, across England, Scotland and Wales on 12 June, his birthday. The aim is to raise more than £1m. "To have their buy-in is wonderful for me," he said.

lead.why: It is the only new England story: the squad will carry Lewis Moody's MND campaign into the All Blacks test.

teams.heading: Laurent Sempéré rules out rotating France's side against Argentina with final in sight
teams.body: Asked whether France would rest players against Argentina with a possible Grand Final at Twickenham to come, France assistant coach Laurent Sempéré said rotation was not something the staff were considering. Every player had shown in training that he could take the jersey, he said, and Saturday's side would be the most competitive available. All players in camp can train, though workloads have been adjusted for those who have played a lot. A bonus-point win over the Pumas would guarantee France's place in the final.

teams.heading: Joe McCarthy says Ireland pack goes into Springboks rematch with 'no fear'
teams.body: Ireland lock Joe McCarthy, who missed the 24-13 defeat by South Africa in November 2025 through injury, told Virgin Media Sport the forwards have "definitely gone hard at it" on the set-piece before Saturday's Nations Championship test in Dublin. In that loss, Springboks head coach Rassie Erasmus' side won penalty after penalty at the scrum, with looseheads Andrew Porter and Paddy McCarthy both yellow-carded. Rather than containing South Africa, the second-row said Ireland will look to attack the game, going in with the mindset that "every contact matters."

lead.why: A new Ireland player story on the scrum rematch, distinct from the Easterby, Sheehan and Kelleher editions already run.

teams.heading: Italy prop Simone Ferrari flags Fiji's physicality before Round 6 test
teams.body: Benetton front-rower Simone Ferrari, one of six props in Italy head coach Gonzalo Quesada's squad, said Fiji have players with great physicality. The Round 6 meeting is Italy's last match of the Nations Championship pool stage. They come into it off the 14-19 defeat by Argentina in Genoa — a fifth loss in five. Ferrari, who has 75 caps, will learn whether he starts when Quesada announces the team on Thursday, with a team run at the Bluenergy Stadium to follow.

lead.why: It is the only new Italy item, a squad player's view of the Fiji test.

teams.heading: Max Williamson says he thrives on physical battle after flattening Harry Wilson
teams.body: Max Williamson made the most of an unplanned outing in Sunday's 15-12 win over Australia at Murrayfield. The Scotland lock came on in the first half when Scott Cummings was forced off injured, and buried Wallabies captain Harry Wilson with a hit. He now says the physical contest is where he is at his best. Cummings has since returned to Glasgow with leg damage and misses Saturday's Japan game. Edinburgh's Grant Gilchrist and Leicester Tigers lock Cam Henderson are among the call-ups.

lead.why: A new Scotland player storyline from the Australia win, not the already-reported injury news.

teams.heading: Wales squad shown fans' reaction to All Blacks win, says Matt Sherratt
teams.body: Head coach Steve Tandy's squad returned to training on Monday, 48 hours after the 35-28 win over New Zealand, having been given time off to enjoy the result with their families. One team meeting included a video of what the victory meant to supporters, and Wales assistant coach Matt Sherratt said: "The boys loved watching some of the videos we've seen, some of the memes online about people's reactions in their living rooms." Attention now turns to Saturday's visit of Australia to Cardiff.

teams.heading: Pumas' Genoa win over Italy draws 314,483 viewers on Italian television
teams.body: Free-to-air channel TV8 accounted for 208,967 of that audience for Argentina's 19-14 Nations Championship win in Genoa, with 89,931 more watching Sky Sport Uno's simulcast and 15,585 on Sky Sport Arena, according to OnRugby. The total topped the 294,345 who saw Italy's meeting with South Africa a week earlier, and dwarfed every other fifth-round fixture on Italian screens — Wales' win over New Zealand drew 60,883. Head coach Felipe Contepomi's side face France in Paris next.

teams.heading: Carter Gordon backs Wallabies to 'flip the switch' on attack against Wales
teams.body: Wallabies fly-half Carter Gordon said wet Murrayfield conditions dragged the 15-12 defeat to Scotland — his Test return after a broken leg in Argentina — into a territory battle, but he is confident the brand built over the past 12 months can return against Wales. He set up wing Harry Potter's early try, yet assistant coach Tom Donnelly said Australia carried too high into Scotland's choke tackles and must get their body height down. Wales arrive off a drought-breaking win over the All Blacks that broke the tackle record.

teams.heading: Japan take fifth Southern Hemisphere spot into Murrayfield group-stage finale
teams.body: Under head coach Eddie Jones, Japan close the Nations Championship group stage on five points. This round's results settle the pairings for the placement finals at Twickenham a week later. Their Murrayfield opponents, Scotland head coach Gregor Townsend's side, edged Australia 15-12 last week and sit fourth in the Northern Hemisphere standings on 15 points. Japan arrive off a 15-78 hammering by England.

teams.heading: Guardian's Kitson says Taylor, McKenzie and Roigard ready to face England
teams.body: Writing in the Guardian, Robert Kitson names Codie Taylor, Damian McKenzie, Cam Roigard and Jordie Barrett among the All Blacks he says are ready for Saturday's test against England at Twickenham. He also says Beauden Barrett and Richie Mo’unga are in the firing line after the 35-28 defeat by Wales. Beauden captained the side for the first time in that match, on his 149th cap, and Kitson says whether he reaches 150 remains to be seen. Kitson notes New Zealand last lost in London and Cardiff on consecutive autumn weekends in 1999.

lead.why: It is the freshest New Zealand-centred story that is not the already-reported Rennie press conference, covering reinforcements and Beauden Barrett's 150th-cap question before England.

teams.heading: SA Rugby Magazine's Mark Keohane says banned Rassie Erasmus betrayed his Springboks
teams.body: Writing in SA Rugby Magazine, Mark Keohane called Springbok head coach Rassie Erasmus's attack on match officials in Dublin "selfish, unprovoked, indulgent and a betrayal of everything he demands of his players." World Rugby has banned Erasmus for six matches, ruling him out of Saturday's Test against Ireland, and SA Rugby has requested a full misconduct hearing. Keohane, who backed Erasmus over his 2021 video criticising referee Nic Berry, pointed instead to a missed levelling conversion and a late front-row change in the 21-19 defeat by France.

lead.why: A leading South African voice turning on Erasmus is the fresh Springbok angle on the ban, from inside the home press.
